title: How to Punt in H2H 9-Cat
brief: When and how should we punt a category in our league, and which categories are good or bad to punt given their stability? It must cover category correlations, why punt rankings mislead, why we should not overpay for punt fits in the auction, and why heavy punting adds variance.
summary: In our 12-team 9-cat league, draft for value first and only lean into a punt once the auction gives you one. Turnovers are the easiest punt. Steals, blocks, threes and FT% are acceptable punts, while points and assists are bad ones. Never pay extra for a player just because he fits your punt, and do not punt so many categories that a low-volume, high-variance roster costs you the playoffs.

sections.heading: What punting is, and when to start

paragraphs.text: Punting means ignoring one or more categories and acting as if they do not exist. It only works in category leagues like ours. It is not a points-league idea. Fantasy value is finite. If you spread it over fewer categories, you get stronger in each one you keep.
Punting is not trying to be bad. You stop caring about the category and move your resources elsewhere. You can still win the punted category in some weeks. That is a bonus, not a goal.

Do not walk into the auction on 2026-10-18 with a fixed punt. Early on, nominate and bid for value. Lean into a punt later only if one appears. If a player goes well below his value, buy him and adjust the build afterwards. Punting is not the only way to win. Value buys and smart waiver moves win leagues too.

A punt is never locked. You can change it mid draft, mid season or mid week. In our league, use the daily FAB waivers (max 6 adds per week) and trades before the 2027-03-04 deadline to shift the build if your roster points somewhere new.

High-variance categories are better to punt: steals, blocks, threes and FT%. You still steal some of them by surprise. Stable, high-volume categories like points and assists are bad to punt. Low-scoring players are hard to build around unless you are fine giving up points.

Turnovers are the easiest punt in head-to-head. Lloyd ignores turnovers in every H2H league, and his Durant ranking for H2H leaves them out. Anyone drafting high-usage, high-value players should punt turnovers because they cannot be avoided. Working hard to keep turnovers low, or to maximize FG%, hurts the rest of the team. Using turnovers as a tiebreaker between two otherwise identical players is fine.
Do not decide to punt FT% because of one bad season from a player. Free throw percentage swings a lot in both directions. Check a longer track record before you treat a player as a punt-FT piece.

Check correlations before you commit. High assists come with high turnovers. Low turnovers come with low points and low assists. High blocks come with high rebounds and high FG%. So if you chase low-block players to punt blocks, your rebounds and FG% will drop as well.
If you punt assists, check your threes, steals and FT%. Low-assist players often struggle there. The upside is that your turnovers fall on their own.

In a punt-FT build, do not roster only bad free throw shooters. Free throws are tied to points, threes and assists, so a team of poor shooters is really punting four categories. After a big man who shoots free throws badly, Giannis being the experts' example, get guard stats (assists, threes, steals) early. Buy guards in two of your next three purchases. Your targets are still every player.

Do not overreact to a weak category either. If assists are thin, do not overindex on chasing them. Do not spend on a one-category specialist to fix a category that is already too weak to recover. Buying a two-category player early also leaves holes you then have to fill.

sections.heading: Punt rankings mislead, so do not overpay

paragraphs.text: Punt rankings lie. They remove your weak category but not everyone else's. That makes punt-fit players look better than they are against real opponents. Lloyd's Durant ranking tries to correct for this.

Overall 9-cat rankings can mislead the other way. If you punt FT%, a player's FT% getting worse barely matters to you, even when his overall rank falls a lot. Read the category line, not just the rank.

In our $200 auction, do not switch on a punt view and pay the inflated punt value. Overpaying for a player because he fits your build is not value. Do not push up bids on players who gain value in punt rankings, such as bad FT% shooters, just to secure them. Set your price from his standard value. Only win him at or below that number.

Heavy punting leaves you with low volume and more variance. That can cost you a playoff spot. With 12 teams, how deep you can punt depends on how many teams make the playoffs. If the top six get in, you can punt more. If only four of 12 get in, a four-category punt may keep you out. Check our playoff bracket size before going beyond one or two punts.

Head-to-head only needs 5 of 9 category wins. Even balanced teams end up punting something in the playoffs. For weeks 19, 20 and 21, ending 2027-03-28, it is fine to drop a category you are losing anyway and stream for the ones you can win.

Cover every position with at least two or three eligible players, even when punting. Our roster has G, G, G, F, F, F, C and three Util spots with daily lineups. If a punt leaves you with one C, you will lose games played during the week.

The experts differ on how central punting should be. One side says punting wins leagues, a weak category is acceptable, and punting gets more viable with more teams, more categories and deeper leagues. That side also says a Giannis-type pick should push you to punt FT%. The other side says people overindex on punting, value and waivers win just as well, and taking Giannis in round one does not force a punt-FT build. For us: let early value decide, and punt only when the roster already leans that way.
